question.problem:
A sports shop sells table tennis balls in boxes of $6.$ The weight of a table tennis ball, in grams, is normally distributed with a mean of $2.72\,\text{g}$ and a standard deviation of $0.05\,\text{g},$ while the weight of a box, in grams, is normally distributed with a mean of $12\,\text{g}$ and a standard deviation of $2\,\text{g}.$ If one box full of balls is randomly selected, what is the probability that it weighs less than $30\,\text{g}?$
You may assume that the weights are mutually independent.

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution.*

| $z$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.04\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.7\,$ | $\,0.7611\,$ | $\,0.7642\,$ | $\,0.7673\,$ | $\,0.7704\,$ |
| $\,0.8\,$ | $\,0.7910\,$ | $\,0.7939\,$ | $\,0.7967\,$ | $\,0.7995\,$ |
| $\,0.9\,$ | $\,0.8186\,$ | $\,0.8212\,$ | $\,0.8238\,$ | $\,0.8264\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Let ${X}_{i}$ denote the weight of the $i$th ball, and let $Y$ denote the weight of a box. Then, we have

$$
{X}_{i}∼N(2.72,{0.05}^{2}),\,1\le i\le 6,
$$

and

$$
Y∼N(12,{2}^{2}).
$$

Let the random variable $W$ denote the weight of a randomly selected box of balls. Then, since

$$
W={X}_{1}+{X}_{2}+⋯+{X}_{6}+Y,
$$

we have that $W$ is normally distributed, where

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[W] & =6\cdot 2.72+12 \\  & =28.32 \\ \text{Var}[W] & =6\cdot {0.05}^{2}+{2}^{2} \\  & =4.015.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
W∼N(28.32,4.015).
$$

In order to find $P(W<30),$ we convert $W$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(W<30) & =P(Z<\frac{30-28.32}{\sqrt{4.015}}) \\  & ≈P(Z<0.84) \\  & =Φ(0.84)\end{aligned}
$$

Using the $z$-table, we see that

$$
Φ(0.84)≈0.7995.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(W<30) & ≈Φ(0.84) \\  & ≈0.7995.\end{aligned}
$$
